strengths: Conquistadors — early firearm unit with high mobility and damage
No Blacksmith upgrades needed — technologies provide equivalent bonuses
Catholic faith advantages — monks stronger and cheaper
Consistent gold income throughout all game ages
weaknesses: Weaker archer line compared to dedicated archer civs
No unique cavalry upgrades — paladin line standard quality only
Infantry options less compelling than specialist civs
Early game relies on careful resource management due to balanced bonuses
unique_unit: Conquistador — mounted crossbowman equivalent, powerful firearm unit effective against both infantry and cavalry

unique_tech.castle_age: Milites Christi — Monks convert faster and have more range
unique_tech.imperial_age: Relics generate gold passively — sustainable late-game economy

economy_bonuses: Lumber camps gather +15% wood starting in Feudal Age
Mining camps gather +20% gold starting in Feudal Age
Relic gold conversion provides passive income stream
team_bonus: Market trade cost reduced — economic synergy for resource-heavy compositions
build_order_notes: Feudal rush with Conquistadors if opponent is vulnerable. Otherwise, steady eco build leveraging wood/gold bonuses. Tech through monasteries for monk pressure or transition to gunpowder. Relics become critical late-game income.
common_pairings: Italians — bankers complement Spanish market trade bonuses
Franks — paladin strength covers Spanish cavalry weakness
Byzantines — anti-cavalry coverage while Spanish focus on firearms and monks

power_spikes.feudal_age: Strong — Conquistadors available early for harassment
power_spikes.castle_age: Very strong — Monastery tech unlocks and firearm pressure peaks
power_spikes.imperial_age: Strong — passive relic income sustains army production indefinitely
